cases.prompt: Explain HTTP 409 Conflict in under 100 words and give one realistic API example. Do not inspect or change this repository.
cases.rubric: Accurately explains a conflict with current resource state, gives a fitting example, respects the word limit, and leaves Git clean.

cases.prompt: In plain English, explain what Promise.allSettled returns when one JavaScript promise rejects. Include a tiny code example. Do not inspect or change files.
cases.rubric: Explains fulfilled and rejected result objects without claiming the aggregate promise rejects; example is valid; Git stays clean.

cases.prompt: Compute Standard API-equivalent cost for 1,000 ordinary input tokens at $2 per million, 400 cached input tokens at $0.20 per million, and 50 output tokens at $10 per million. Show the arithmetic. No repository work.
cases.rubric: Computes $0.00258 total, keeps token categories separate, and leaves Git clean.

cases.prompt: Locate how Pace computes a session project key. Name the function and file, explain Windows path casing and the hash algorithm, and do not change files.
cases.rubric: Identifies projectKey and normalizeProject in src/core/sessions.ts, lowercase Windows absolute path, SHA-256 key, and clean Git.

cases.prompt: Trace where Pace starts and verifies its Vex MCP connection before an auto-routed turn. Name the key functions and files. Do not edit.
cases.rubric: Accurately locates VexRouter.start/verify and the turn entry path, distinguishes startup from per-turn ping, and leaves Git clean.

cases.prompt: Trace how Codex token usage reaches Pace's terminal usage bar. Include the event source, aggregation, and render component. Do not modify files.
cases.rubric: Names the SDK turn.completed usage, orchestrator or turn summary aggregation, and UsageBar rendering path accurately; Git stays clean.

cases.prompt: Inspect the CLI doctor command and relevant tests. Give an actionable plan for adding a --json option that preserves text output. Stop after the plan; do not edit files.
cases.rubric: Plan references real CLI and test seams, covers all existing doctor checks and text compatibility, and leaves Git clean.

cases.prompt: Inspect session persistence and validation. Propose a backward-compatible plan for versioning session files, including rollback and tests. Do not implement.
cases.rubric: Plan identifies current session read/write paths, old-file compatibility, version validation, rollback, and focused tests; Git stays clean.

cases.prompt: Add a --json option to pace doctor that prints one parseable object with every existing check, including Vex and Codex SDK. Preserve current text output and add a focused test.
cases.rubric: JSON parses and covers all checks, default text output remains usable, focused test exists, and build/tests pass.

cases.prompt: Make Pace configuration reject duplicate reasoning effort entries for one model instead of silently deduplicating them. Preserve valid configs and add a focused test.
cases.rubric: Duplicate efforts cause a clear parseConfig error, unique efforts remain valid, focused test exists, and build/tests pass.

cases.prompt: Reject saved session token usage with negative, non-finite, or cache-exceeds-input counts. Preserve loading of valid old sessions. Add focused regression tests.
cases.rubric: Malformed counts are rejected without crashing session listing, valid usage still loads, regression tests cover the cases, and build/tests pass.

cases.prompt: Add a --json form of pace --version that prints a parseable object containing the version. Preserve the existing plain-text version output and cover both forms with a focused test.
cases.rubric: --version --json prints one valid JSON object with version, plain --version output remains, focused test exists, and build/tests pass.
